core_question: Can the original EOG claims about viability, reachability, occurrence-to-occurrence connection, pathwise environmental continuity, barriers, stepping stones, bottlenecks, alternative distribution histories, and robust impossibility be recovered under known truth without forcing a unique history?
not_the_question: how many BAM decompositions exist for their own sake
whether finite partition algebra is novel
whether another synthetic BAM factorial improves the previous target-quotient pattern

world_components.H: directed transition-history structure including sources, stepping stones, branching and bottlenecks

canonical_virtual_archetypes.truth_contrast: same local A at target, different M because a barrier disconnects the target

canonical_virtual_archetypes.purpose: test pathwise IBE rather than endpoint-only environmental similarity
canonical_virtual_archetypes.truth_contrast: source and target environments are similar but every continuous path crosses an environmentally nonviable intermediate state

canonical_virtual_archetypes.purpose: test whether an intermediate occurrence can make a route possible when direct movement is impossible
canonical_virtual_archetypes.truth_contrast: same endpoints; one world contains a viable stepping stone and one does not

canonical_virtual_archetypes.purpose: test route redundancy and vulnerability to one critical edge/node
canonical_virtual_archetypes.truth_contrast: same observed endpoint set; one world has a single bottleneck, another has two independent routes

canonical_virtual_archetypes.purpose: test set-valued world reconstruction instead of unique history recovery
canonical_virtual_archetypes.truth_contrast: two source/branching histories yield the same final occurrence set G but different source attribution / first-passage structure

canonical_virtual_archetypes.purpose: test whether time-stamped occurrence history contracts static ambiguity
canonical_virtual_archetypes.truth_contrast: worlds share final G but differ in admissible arrival order

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one target is locally viable in every candidate world but reachable only in a strict subset of worlds.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if local viability always implies reachability in all canonical archetypes.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Endpoint environmental similarity alone can misclassify a source-target pair as connectable when every admissible path contains an environmental bottleneck.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if endpoint-only and pathwise-environmental rules never disagree in V2.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: A predeclared stepping stone can convert an otherwise unreachable source-target pair into a reachable pair without changing endpoint local viability.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if V3 reachability is invariant to the stepping-stone state.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Two worlds can support the same observed occurrences while differing in edge/node knockout sensitivity and route redundancy.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if V4 worlds with the same observed support have identical knockout and redundancy signatures.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one final occurrence set is compatible with multiple source/branching histories that differ in source attribution or first-passage structure.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if every canonical final G identifies one history world.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Time-stamped positive occurrence order strictly contracts at least one static-compatible history fiber while retaining the true world.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if temporal positive evidence never contracts static ambiguity.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: When the candidate-world universe is expanded, robustly impossible occurrence relations can only be lost, never newly created, while possible relations can only be gained.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any violation is an implementation/theory failure and stops interpretation.

primary_outputs: robust / contingent / impossible occurrence-pair relation matrix
success_definition: The programme succeeds if the original EOG claims are either supported or falsified under known truth with explicit counterexamples and without promoting one compatible history to truth.
stop_rules: Do not add archetypes after scoring to rescue a failed hypothesis.
Do not tune barriers, stepping-stone states, environmental gaps or timing after scoring.
Do not claim that synthetic support establishes empirical truth.
Do not collapse multiple compatible histories into one best route.
Do not replace this programme with BAM decomposition counting alone.
Do not use the frozen EOG-WF empirical denominator to tune these virtual worlds.
